newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX ends at 6th successive closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX ends at 6th successive closing high.

text.p: A five-day string of record closes on the Budapest Stock Exchange continued on Friday as demand absorbed shares unloaded by arbitrageurs between the cash and the futures markets, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 6,319.01 points, up 60.76.
"There were those who stepped out from arbitrage, but there was support on the buying side," said Zsolt Madacsi of ING Barings, adding foreigners were on the buying side.
Accordingly BUX futures traded firmer, with the June maturity, which expires on June 16, advancing to 6,320 points in the last deal from Thursday's settlement price of 6,242.50.

Market participants expected the market's positive tone to remain, pending the dollar remaining firm. A strong dollar makes Hungarian shares cheaper to foreign investors, the main players of the market.
"If the dollar retains its levels the market will be positive and prices may rise further with a few exceptions," Madacsi said.
Friday's gainers included pharmaceuticals Egis Rt which put on 300 forints to end at 11,700 and oil company MOL Rt which gained 70 forints to 3,615.

Machinery firm Mezogep Rt retained its record-breaking form which accelerated after the company released its Q1 figures earlier this week. It closed at a new high of 2,850 forints, up 150, in not particularly strong volume.
Analysts said the Hungarian government's decision on Thursday to reduce its stakes to "golden shares" in key firms will have a beneficial impact on longer term.

"The government's decision to bring down state shareholdings to the lowest level possible in what were previously considered strategic companies will be an important step," said Spencer Jakab, analyst at CS First Boston in Budapest.
